title: Basic-auth job search must be narrowed to the caller's own jobs
answers: non-admin user sees other users' jobs in job search under basic-auth
POST /ajax-api/3.0/jobs/search returns every job to any authenticated user
users can enumerate other users' job ids, params and results through job search
why does jobs search return jobs created by other accounts
body:
Symptom: under --app-name basic-auth, a non-admin calling job search gets every job in the store, including other users' params and result/error text, while GET of the same job id returns 403.
Root cause: mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_get_job_route_validator only requires authentication for the search path, so the full result of the search handler reaches the caller.
Fix pattern: keep the Job response model exposing creator (mlflow/server/job_api.py:Job.from_job_entity) and register mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_filter_search_jobs in FASTAPI_ENDPOINT_RESPONSE_FILTERS keyed on job_api.search_jobs, keeping only jobs whose creator equals the username.
Constraints: the filter runs after the response, which is only sound because the search handler returns the full unpaginated set; a paginated or store-side search must filter in the query instead. Jobs with no creator (legacy rows, worker-spawned child jobs) stay hidden from non-admins, matching the per-id routes. Admins skip response filters in fastapi_permission_middleware.
Applies: the basic-auth native FastAPI job search route and any new job listing route.
applies: basic-auth FastAPI job collection routes; not the per-id get/cancel routes, which are gated by ownership in the validator.
says: Standard users can see other accounts' background jobs, parameters, and results in job search.
Restrict the jobs dashboard view so team members only see their own submitted tasks.
Non-administrator accounts are able to view private execution results from other people's jobs.
Filter the background job search list to display only jobs created by the caller.
search: Under basic-auth, job search responses must be filtered to return only jobs belonging to the authenticated caller. _filter_search_jobs in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py is registered in FASTAPI_ENDPOINT_RESPONSE_FILTERS for job_api.search_jobs, matching the username against the creator field exposed by Job.from_job_entity. This post-response filter applies because the handler returns an unpaginated set, whereas paginated or store-side searches must filter within the database query. Administrator accounts bypass response filters in fastapi_permission_middleware, while jobs lacking a creator stay hidden from non-admins, applying to FastAPI job search and listing routes.
